fields.title: Meaning as a number
fields.keyTakeaway: Vector search is good for meaning and bad for exact matches, numbers, and negations, so it is supplemented with filters and text search.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: How does search find "lactose-free milk" for the query "dairy for intolerance"?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Vector search feels like magic and is therefore either overestimated or underestimated. Understanding the mechanics at a metaphorical level is enough to predict where it will work.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: **[[embedding|Embedding]]** is the representation of text as a set of numbers. Texts close in meaning get close sets. The measure of closeness is the distance between them.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: Metaphor: each text gets coordinates in a semantic space. "Milk" and "kefir" are close. "Milk" and "drill" are far apart.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **[[vector-search|Vector search]]** turns a query into an embedding and finds the nearest ones. Hence the ability to find by meaning without word matches.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: *Synonyms and paraphrases.* "Lactose intolerance" finds "lactose-free". *Semantic closeness.* "Something for breakfast" finds cereal and yogurt. *Different languages,* if the embedding model is multilingual.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: *Exact matches.* SKU codes, brand names, numbers. For the model, "Domik v derevne" and "Prostokvashino" are almost identical. *Negations.* "Milk without sugar" and "milk with sugar" are very close in semantic space because they differ by one word. This is a regular trap. *Numerical conditions.* "Cheaper than 200 rubles" cannot be expressed by meaning — a filter is needed. *Freshness and priorities.* An embedding does not know that one document is newer than another.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Hence the rule: **vector search complements traditional search, it does not replace it.** Numerical and exact conditions are handled by filters and text search, meaning by vectors.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Three cases that defined the search architecture.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *Works.* "Something for tea" finds cookies, candy, jam. No shared words at all.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: *Does not work without help.* "Milk without palm oil" found milk with palm oil with the same probability. Solved by a metadata filter on ingredients plus an explicit rule in the model instruction to check for negation.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: *Does not work at all.* "Prostokvashino 3.2%" — vector search returned any milk of that fat content. Solved by hybrid search: the text part catches the brand.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Negations turned out to be the most frequent cause of incorrect answers after chunking. We introduced a rule: if the query contains "without", "not", "except", additional ingredient filtering is applied, and the model receives an explicit instruction to check.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Embedding quality depends on the model, and for narrow domains, general models perform worse. This must be tested on your own data, not on promises.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Vector search is good for meaning and bad for exact matches, numbers, and negations, so it is supplemented with filters and text search.
